messages:
maria_support: Customer 24321 opened a ticket — they get a 403 when calling /v1/generate with their API key. They think it's an auth token/scope issue because the error text says 'insufficient_scope'. Customer insists the key is valid and works for other endpoints. They attached a curl and response. Can eng take a look?

maria_support: curl they ran: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-live-abc123\" \ 
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \ 
  -d '{"model":"codegen-alpha","prompt":"print(\"hi\")"}'```

maria_support: Response body: ```{\n  "error": { "type": "forbidden", "message": "insufficient_scope: missing scope 'model.codegen'", "status": 403 }\n}```

maria_support: customer account id: acct_24321. Says they were on Starter but recently trialed a Pro add-on. No billing alerts on our side.

raj_engineer: looking. At first glance old middleware returns generic 'insufficient_scope' for any 403 coming out of entitlement checks. If the entitlement service says model not allowed, we bubble up the auth-style message.

raj_engineer: can you paste the X-Request-ID from the customer or their raw headers? need to trace in ingress logs.

maria_support: they gave request-id: req_20260314_5f7a. Full headers they sent: ```accept: application/json
authorization: Bearer sk-live-abc123
x-account-id: acct_24321```

raj_engineer: traced it. Sequence: API gateway -> auth middleware (valid key) -> plan check service returns DENY for model 'codegen-alpha' because acct_24321 is on Starter and codegen is Pro-only feature. The plan-check call returns {allowed:false, reason:'plan_limit'}. Our middleware maps that to a generic 403 with message 'insufficient_scope'.

raj_engineer: So it's not an OAuth scope missing, it's a plan gating result. The problem: UX and the message confuse customers and support. We should return a clearer error code/message (e.g., 403 with code 'plan_blocked' and copy 'feature codegen-alpha not on your plan — upgrade to Pro or request access').

carl_support: customer says they recently toggled Pro trial and expected it to be immediate. Could be eventual consistency between billing and entitlement. Any ideas how long plan changes take?

sophie_prod: Plan activation should be near-real-time for most cases, but the entitlement cache is updated on a 30s poll in most regions. If they flipped a trial less than 30s before the request it could be stale. Also some payment triggers run async. We need to check order of operations for trial events.

raj_engineer: confirmed: entitlement-service shows acct_24321 in state 'pro_pending' at time of request. So two issues: (1) stale cache allowed us to evaluate against old plan and (2) messaging is misleading.

raj_engineer: Immediate mitigation options:
- Update middleware to detect plan_check reason 'plan_limit' and emit a friendly message that includes account plan and required feature.
- Add a backoff/retry in the SDK sample when 403 with 'plan_pending' is returned.
- Support can advise customer to wait 60s and retry, or verify billing page shows active Pro.

maria_support: I'll tell the customer: "Looks like your trial was still pending when that request hit us — please wait ~1m and retry, and if you still see it send request-id." Want to include a short copy for support message.

carl_support: suggested reply draft: "Thanks — we see the request hit while your Pro trial was still pending, which triggered a plan restriction. This returns a 403 that looks like an auth error; please retry after a minute and let us know if it persists. If you need immediate access we can escalate to enable feature for you." Good?

maria_support: perfect, sending.

raj_engineer: longer-term: I'll open a tiny patch to the middleware to change the error shape. Proposal: response body should include fields: code: 'plan_blocked' | 'plan_pending', plan: 'Starter', required: 'codegen-alpha', help_url. Also add a monitoring alert for 'insufficient_scope' messages that originate from plan checks (so we can measure how often customers are confused).

sophie_prod: +1. Also we should add a one-line note in docs / errors page explaining plan-gating vs auth scopes. I'll file a doc ticket.

deploy-bot: build #3582 passed for repo services/entitlement; patch branch plan-error-clarify is ready for review.

raj_engineer: I'll open PR and ping @sre for quick canary. Plan to roll patch today.

maria_support: customer replied after 90s and confirmed retry succeeded. They were able to call /v1/generate without 403. I'll close ticket once devs confirm patch lands.

sophie_prod: created PROD-UX-112 in product board for docs + error catalog update.

raj_engineer: PR link: https://git.internal.redwood/repo/pulls/212. Changes include mapping plan_check reasons to error codes and adding help_url pointing at the errors doc.

maria_support: thanks all — marking thread resolved from support side but keeping open for deploy confirmation.

raj_engineer: deploy completed to canary at 1785240000; no regressions. Will promote to prod after 30m.

maria_support: confirmed customer closed their side. I'll post update to #support-ops after full roll.

carl_support: quick note — let's add a KB snippet: '403 that looks like missing scope but is actually plan gated' to the support handbook. Saves time.

maria_support: adding KB now.
